Data only: this page has no written analysis. Every number below is computed from the ledger's data tables and carries a source and a retrieval date in the figures file. Tables retrieved 2026-10-10.

This ledger starts in fiscal 2010 (July 2009), the first year Massachusetts put its spending records online. Penalties, donations and lobbying before then are left out so every comparison covers the same years.

State and federal donation totals are never added together. Donations are gifts by individuals who report the company as employer; they are not company money. Appearing in several of these records is an overlap in the records, not evidence that one led to another.

sections.heading: Penalties
sections.html:
How penalty amounts are counted: each row counts the cash the defendant actually paid (penalties, restitution, damages, fees). Press-release headline figures are often larger because they include debt relief, forgiven debt or rent, bill credits, conditional amounts, or proposed penalties that can still be contested. Those parts are not counted here. Every one is listed under Amounts not counted, with the headline figure, what we counted, the reason and the source. Where a release does not state the split between cash and relief, the case is left out of the totals and listed there.

How duplicates are counted: when two records describe the same payment, it is counted once. A record is left out only when a primary document read for this ledger shows the dollars are the same. When that document cannot be read, a strong match is still counted once and is marked 'possible duplicate, counted once until verified'. Records for different payments are all counted, even when the amounts are equal. Every record left out stays in the gross figure and is listed under Amounts not counted, with the document behind the call.

How shared totals are counted: when several defendants pay one total, each company counts only the share its primary document states. If the document gives a total and no split, and the payers include anyone outside the one company (another company, or individuals such as owners), the total is counted for no company: it stays in the gross figure and is listed under Amounts not counted. Where every payer named belongs to the one company, the whole total counts once, in full, for that company.

No amount in this company's penalty records is left out under these rules.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.html:
• The window starts in fiscal 2010 (July 2009). Older records are not in this file.
  • Donors are matched to the company by the employer they report. Donors who left the field blank or wrote self-employed are missed, so the counted donations are a floor for what the matching can see.
  • Probable matches are excluded from every total: 0 OCPF and 0 FEC row(s) for this company. Held matches (reviewed and undecided) are not counted. 0 OCPF and 0 FEC confirmed rows are left out as in-kind, memo entries or pass-throughs.
  • Named individuals are not linked on profile pages.
  • Lobbying firm fees in the table start in 2010. In-house lobbying costs (the company's own staff lobbyists) are entered only from 2025, so for earlier years the lobbying figure is firm fees only. Statements of Financial Interest cover 2019 to 2025.
  • Newest period in the tables: penalties 2016-03-07; state donations none on record; federal donations 2013-04-09; lobbying none on record; holdings none on record; contracts fiscal 2019. A penalty announced after the table date is not in the ledger.
  • Totals are nominal dollars.

window.note: Fiscal 2010 is the first year of the state's online spending records; every stream uses the same start.

penalties.note: Government penalties only; private lawsuits are not rows. HQ-lens rows start at the company's Massachusetts headquarters date.

contracts.note: Net payments by fiscal year; the newest fiscal year is partial. Payers: CTHRU, MBTA, MASSPORT, MSBA.

donations_ocpf.note: Confirmed employer matches, cash, memo entries and pass-throughs left out. State totals; never summed with FEC.

donations_fec.note: Confirmed employer matches, cash, memo entries and pass-throughs left out. Federal totals; never summed with OCPF.

lobbying.note: Firm fees (what a company paid outside lobbying firms) from 2010; in-house lobbying costs (a company's own staff lobbyists) exist only for 2025 and 2026, so before 2025 the lobbying total is firm fees only. 2010-2015 firm fees were read from the Secretary's public search pages on 2026-10-11.

holdings.note: Annual disclosure filings; confirmed matches only.
